| [THEORY-017](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-017.md) v7 | Hilbert-space parts are extra data, not intrinsic | Carroll (2021), [LIT-123](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-123.md): a quantum theory is fixed up to unitary equivalence by the Hamiltonian's spectrum, and subsystems come from a factorisation that the dynamics must select. Van Rijsbergen ([LIT-262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-262.md)) computes only traces and inner products, and treats each observable's eigenbasis as a "point of view". DisCoCat's ε/η composition ([LIT-273](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-273.md)) is orthogonally covariant, while its Frobenius sequel ([LIT-272](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-272.md)) stipulates a basis and composes by elementwise product in it. [THEORY-004](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-004.md) is the same point for learned representations. This is a synthesis across the four, not a result any one of them states. It does not say that basis-dependent models are wrong; it says what they have assumed. | Active |
| [THEORY-261](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-261.md) v3 | SDM capacity scales with hard locations | Kanerva (1992), [LIT-921](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-921.md), §§3.5–3.7, read in full in [NOTE-779](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-779.md), after Jaeckel (1989a). An approximate derivation for uniform random data and exact retrieval cues. It does not cover noisy cues, which lower capacity, or clustered data, which the uniform design handles badly, and it does not contain the critical-distance analysis that is sometimes attributed to it. | Active |
| [THEORY-361](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-361.md) | Top-k under min needs ~n/2 accesses at worst | Fagin, Lotem and Naor (2001; full version read as arXiv cs/0204046v1), [LIT-1115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1115.md), read in [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md): Example 6.3 and Theorem 6.4, the paper's proof that no algorithm is instance optimal once lucky lookups are allowed. With 2n + 1 objects, n + 1 high in each list and only one high in both, an algorithm that cannot guess must read at least n + 1 entries before it sees the target, and on a randomized family any deterministic algorithm needs at least n + 1 accesses in expectation. The paper uses the case to bound instance optimality. That it explains linear conjunction-search slopes in human vision is the record's analogy, not the paper's claim. | Active |
| [THEORY-363](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-363.md) | Threshold algorithm is instance optimal | Fagin, Lotem and Naor (2001; full version read as arXiv cs/0204046v1), [LIT-1115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1115.md), read in [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md). The threshold algorithm reads m attribute-sorted lists in parallel, looks up each new object's other grades, and stops when k seen objects score at least the combined score of the last grades read. For every monotone combining function it is instance optimal among correct algorithms that make no wild guesses (Theorem 6.1), with ratio m + m(m−1)c_R/c_S, tight for strict functions (Corollary 6.2, Theorem 9.1). It is a guarantee relative to a class of algorithms under an access-cost model. It does not say that top-k queries are cheap: the absolute cost depends on the data, and is linear in N for some conjunctive queries. | Active |
| [THEORY-365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-365.md) v4 | HNSW cost grew logarithmically in uniform tests | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md) from arXiv v4. They build an index like a skip list, with proximity graphs in place of linked lists, and argue that search costs a constant per layer over O(log N) layers. That holds if each layer is an exact Delaunay graph of bounded mean degree. HNSW does not build such graphs, and Delaunay degree grows exponentially with dimension. For the graphs it does build, cost no worse than logarithmic is measured on uniform random data at d = 8, a saturating beam width at d = 4, and at d = 128 (200M SIFT) the growth departs from a logarithm. A proof for the graphs HNSW builds is QUESTION-187. The paper gives no worst-case bound and no recall guarantee. Construction is argued to cost about N searches. | Active |
| [THEORY-366](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-366.md) | Concentrated distances make nearest ≈ farthest | Beyer, Goldstein, Ramakrishnan and Shaft (1999), [LIT-1099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1099.md), read in [NOTE-917](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-917.md) from the authors' 1998 technical report. Theorem 1: for n fixed data points and an independent query, var(d^p / E[d^p]) → 0 implies P[DMAX ≤ (1+ε)DMIN] → 1 for every ε > 0. The index m is arbitrary, so dimension enters only through the workload's distance distributions. IID coordinates and several correlated or non-identical workloads satisfy the condition; a diagonal line, two latent degrees of freedom and queries inside clusters do not. The condition is sufficient, not necessary. The result concerns the ratio of distances at fixed n, and does not show that real high-dimensional data loses contrast, or that indexes fail. | Active |
| [THEORY-368](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-368.md) v3 | Graph ANN indexes fail on adversarial 2D sets | Indyk and Xu (2023), [LIT-1112](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1112.md), read in [NOTE-910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-910.md). The instances are grids of points in the plane in which a large cluster, reached first from the start vertex, lies closer to the query than the only points linked to its nearest neighbour. At queue length 0.1n, average recall@5 ranged from 0.0 (DiskANN) to 0.42 (KGraph). The paper calls the query time linear and says so "empirically"; the only argument beyond the experiment is an informal Ω(n/R) for DiskANN's fast build. It does not show that these indexes fail on natural data or natural queries. | Active |
| [THEORY-369](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-369.md) v2 | Partitioning NN indexes lose to scans in high dim | Weber, Schek and Blott (1998), [LIT-1107](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1107.md), read in [NOTE-919](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-919.md). Under uniformity and independence, with the expected nearest-neighbour distance used as every query's radius and integrals evaluated by Monte Carlo, the fraction of blocks read passes the 20% line at about d = 15–20 for rectangular regions and 26 for spherical ones. A crude bound for any convex clustering puts it below 610. The often-quoted "around 10" is the measured crossover for an R*-tree and an X-tree. The VA-file, a scan of compact per-vector approximations, is the paper's alternative. Nothing is shown for data of low intrinsic dimension, and the finite-dimensional bounds are not rigorous as stated. The asymptotic statement, at fixed N and for clusters of two or more points, is proved by the record by a concentration argument. | Active |
| [THEORY-370](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-370.md) | Small-world search is fast only at r = 2 | Kleinberg (2000), [LIT-1103](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1103.md), read in [NOTE-923](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-923.md). Proved for the two-dimensional lattice: with nodes, local links and the number of long-range links fixed, changing only the exponent r of the long-range link distribution moves the expected delivery time of the best decentralized searcher from O((log n)²) at r = 2 to a power of n at every other r, including r = 0, where paths of polylogarithmic length exist. The upper bound is proved only for one local and one long-range link per node; the k-dimensional statement (r = k) is asserted, not proved; the family is inverse power laws of a distance every node can compute, so it does not show that no other link structure is navigable. | Active |
| [THEORY-372](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-372.md) | ANN space–time trade-off is optimal for hashing | Andoni, Laarhoven, Razenshteyn and Waingarten (2017), [LIT-1120](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1120.md), read in [NOTE-918](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-918.md) from the arXiv full version. A data-dependent tree of spherical caps, with different thresholds for filing points and for routing queries, realizes every pair of exponents on the curve, for worst-case data, with constant success probability; the equal-threshold point is LSH. On random instances with d = ω(log n), list-of-points structures cannot beat the curve (a lower bound the paper calls conditional), and one- or two-probe cell-probe structures need n^{(c/(c−1))²−o(1)} words, the curve's space at ρq = 0. Optimality for data-dependent schemes, for more probes, and for d = Θ(log n) is not shown. The curve prices space against per-query time for one query at a time; it has no workload and no build cost beyond space. | Active |
| [THEORY-376](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-376.md) v3 | Semantic caching answers queries partly locally | Dar, Franklin, Jónsson, Srivastava and Tan (1996), [LIT-1113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1113.md), read in [NOTE-904](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-904.md). In one simulator (one client, one server, a 10,000-tuple relation, 90% of queries in a hot 10%), semantic caching performed about like page caching on a clustered index, far better on an unclustered one, and on an unindexed attribute answered over 60% of 1% queries with no server scan. Space overhead depended on coalescing: 55 regions and about 275 factors for 1% queries without it. The result is measured, not proved; updates, joins and the CPU cost of reasoning about the cache's contents were left out, so it does not show that predicate-described storage pays when finding the reusable part is costly. | Active |
| [THEORY-379](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-379.md) v3 | FA top-k is sublinear for independent lists | Fagin (1996/1999), [LIT-1108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1108.md), as reported by Fagin, Lotem and Naor (2001), [LIT-1115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1115.md), read in [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md). Fagin's own paper could not be obtained, and the reporting paper declines to describe the probability model ("off track"). It does correct one misreading: the only probabilistic assumption is independence of the lists' orderings, not a uniform distribution of grades. For two lists the bound is √(Nk). It does not hold for anti-correlated attributes, where any algorithm can need about half the objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-384](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-384.md) | α-pruned graphs make greedy NN search provable | Indyk and Xu (2023), [LIT-1112](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1112.md), read in [NOTE-910](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-910.md). Proved for DiskANN's "slow preprocessing" build, not the build DiskANN implements. The guarantee rests on one property of the graph (α-shortcut reachability, α > 1), gives a constant approximation, not exact search, is logarithmic in the aspect ratio ∆, which can exceed n by far, and has a per-step cost exponential in the doubling dimension. HNSW and NSG prune with α = 1 and are not covered. | Active |
| [THEORY-385](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-385.md) v3 | HNSW heuristic links keep clustered data reachable | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md). In HNSW, each new element's neighbours are chosen either as its M nearest candidates or by a pruning rule that keeps a candidate only if it is nearer the new element than to any neighbour already kept, a rule related to the relative neighbourhood graph. On 10M random d = 10 vectors in 100 isolated clusters, nearest-neighbour links failed to reach high recall and the pruning rule did not. In every test reported, the rule was at least as good. Its gain was largest at low dimension, at high recall, and on clustered data, and small on uniform or very high-dimensional data. These are the authors' benchmarks: one clustered dataset, synthetic, with no independent replication in this reading. Re-run independently at smaller scale on promotion (2026-10-20), with the same result. | Active |
| [THEORY-388](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-388.md) | LSH gives sublinear approximate NN queries | Indyk and Motwani (1998), [LIT-1106](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1106.md), read in [NOTE-905](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-905.md) from the authors' 1999 expanded version, compared with the STOC text. A hash family under which points within r1 collide with probability at least p1 and points beyond r2 with at most p2 gives n^ρ random tables, each storing every point: O(dn + n^{1+ρ}) space and O(n^ρ) hash evaluations per query, ρ = ln(1/p1)/ln(1/p2), for the decision version, which ring-cover trees connect to approximate nearest neighbour with polylog overhead. Bit sampling gives ρ ≤ 1/(1+ε) in Hamming space and, by embedding, ℓ_p for p in [1, 2]; the STOC text states 1/ε and only for ε > 1. Grid bucketing gives Õ(d) queries for n·O(1/ε)^d preprocessing. Preprocessing is counted as space. Nothing is proved about whether these exponents can be beaten. | Active |
| [THEORY-480](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-480.md) v2 | Google must share search data, not models | Mehta (2025), [LIT-006](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-006.md), the remedies opinion, read in full in [NOTE-004](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-004.md). The court finds that exclusive distribution produced a scale advantage (9× the queries of all rivals; 93% of unique phrases seen only by Google), calls it a fruit of the violation, and remedies it with raw data and syndication rather than with divestiture, on a sliding scale of causal connection. Whether the shared data will let rivals compete is untested; the parameters that decide it were left to a Technical Committee. The opinion also finds no proof that search scale gives Google's GenAI a quality edge (op. p. 156), which is an absence of proof, not a finding that there is none. | Active |
| [THEORY-697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-697.md) | Attention approximates SDM reads only locally | Bricken & Pehlevan (2021), [LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md), read in full in [NOTE-242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-242.md), which re-evaluated the intersection formula and the fit. The exact intersection (Eq. 2) is checked against Kanerva's lune formula and simulation; eight SDM and fitted-softmax variants retrieve almost identically on random patterns, MNIST and CIFAR-10, with three named exceptions. The intersection is a staircase in distance, the fit holds to about dv = 20 for d = 15, the analytic β of App. B.2 is about 2–2.5 times too small, and every optimal radius assumes random patterns and addresses. The GPT-2 "confirmation" and the cerebellar implementation of attention are argument, not demonstration. | Active |
| [THEORY-815](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-815.md) | Hierarchical NSW gives logarithmic search cost | Malkov and Yashunin (2020), [LIT-1098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1098.md), read in [NOTE-916](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-916.md), argue that HNSW's hierarchy is what makes greedy search logarithmic: constant cost per layer over O(log N) layers, against the polylogarithmic cost of their earlier flat graph. The record holds as measured, in [THEORY-365](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-365.md), logarithmic-or-better cost on uniform data in 8 dimensions and a saturating beam width in 4. The bound is derived only for exact Delaunay layers, which HNSW does not build, and on 200 million SIFT vectors the paper's own scaling departs from a logarithm, so the thesis is stated for low intrinsic dimension. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-832](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-832.md) | Fagin's Algorithm is optimal for independent lists | Fagin (1996/1999), [LIT-1108](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1108.md), as reported by Fagin, Lotem and Naor (2001), [LIT-1115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1115.md), Sections 1 and 3, read in [NOTE-924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-924.md): "his algorithm is optimal with high probability in the worst case if the aggregation function is strict ... and if the orderings in the sorted lists are probabilistically independent." | [THEORY-969](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-969.md) v2 | hLDA documents draw from a single tree path | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). hLDA's overlap between documents is nested by construction: at each level of the tree the documents are partitioned, and a document can share topics with two others only if one of the two shares all of its shared topics with it. It is a statement about the model, not about the data, and it says nothing about whether the tree the sampler finds is identified. The multiple-path relaxation is the nested HDP's ([LIT-002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-002.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-989](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-989.md) | hLDA beats flat LDA on held-out JACM abstracts | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), §6.3 and Fig. 9, read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). One corpus, five-fold cross-validation, hyperparameters integrated out. It is evidence that a single-path hierarchy can earn its constraint in prediction, near its own size. It is not evidence that a hierarchy predicts better than a flat mixed-membership model in general: the paper itself says the flat model should dominate at large topic counts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1003](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1003.md) | Author–topic beats LDA only on short documents | Rosen-Zvi, Chemudugunta, Griffiths, Smyth and Steyvers (2010), [LIT-1546](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1546.md), §6.4 and Fig. 11, read in [NOTE-1180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1180.md). Pooling by member helps prediction of a document of which little has been seen and costs it once the document's own words are enough. One corpus, one split, one topic count. It is not evidence that member-level structure is real, only that it predicts in a regime of sparse evidence. | Active |

| [THEORY-1656](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1656.md) | LLM documents crowd out human sources in retrieval | Yu, Kim and Kim (2026), read in [NOTE-1752](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1752.md) (Read). The authors name "Retrieval Collapse", a two-stage failure in which (1) AI-generated content comes to dominate search results, eroding source diversity, and (2) low-quality or adversarial synthetic content enters the retrieval pipeline. On 1,000 MS MARCO queries, each with ten Google-retrieved web documents (Original Pool), they add GPT-5-nano documents one per round for 20 rounds (pool contamination 0% → 66.7%), in two scenarios: an "SEO" pool (LLM rewrites of original documents with high-IDF keywords) and an "Abuse" pool (clickbait drafts with named entities and numbers falsified). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1677](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1677.md) | Recommenders both erode and aid authenticity | Étienne Brown, read in [NOTE-1792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1792.md) (Read). Brown argues that recommender systems affect users' capacity to be their authentic selves, both negatively and positively. He offers a "minimal", multi-dimensional account of authenticity with two dimensions: volitional alignment (Frankfurt, via Rings: acting on first-order desires one reflectively endorses at second order) and self-understanding (an epistemic dimension, relational rather than purely introspective: others' testimony and recommendations are a source of self-knowledge). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1695](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1695.md) | Information voids clustered at vaccine rollout | Scalco, Gesualdo, Cerqueti and Cinelli (2026), read in [NOTE-1748](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1748.md) (Read). Treating the online information ecosystem as a market with information **demand** (Wikipedia page views, Google Trends) and **supply** (Facebook posts via CrowdTangle, Twitter full-archive, GDELT news volume), the authors rescale each series by its mean, define an information delta δt = ŝt − d̂t, decompose δ by STL and flag remainder outliers by an IQR rule. Anomalies with δ < 0 are **voids** (demand far exceeds supply), δ > 0 **overabundance**; a five-regime scale runs Void / Lack / Balance / Abundance / Overabundance. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1697](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1697.md) | Org-aware recommender cuts workshop imbalance | Davoudabadi, Makui and Rasouli, read in [NOTE-1740](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1740.md) (Read). The authors propose a recommender that scores each candidate item for a user by combining (a) a user-side score and (b) an organization-side score. User side: a reference point built from the user's peak and most recent purchase utilities (peak-end rule), item distances to it split into gains and losses with a prospect-theory-style value function (the EXPTODIM method), and a "user flexibility" index from the diversity of the user's past purchases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1701](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1701.md) | Platform quality collapse can be irreversible | Montero-Porras, Smets and Lenaerts (2026), Enshittification of Algorithmic Recommendation: An Evolutionary Model of Platform-Creator Dynamics, read in [NOTE-1787](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1787.md) (Read). A two-population evolutionary game between a platform (x = probability its recommender rewards costly quality content) and creators (y = probability a creator invests in quality), under replicator dynamics: ẋ = x(1−x)(Ry−A), ẏ = y(1−y)(Vx−C). With R > A and V > C there are two stable pure equilibria, (1,1) "virtuous" and (0,0) "vicious", separated by an interior saddle at (x*, y*) = (C/V, A/R). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1705](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1705.md) | No-regret recommenders erode producer effort | Incentivizing High-Quality Content in Online Recommender Systems (Hu, Jagadeesan, Jordan, Steinhardt), read in [NOTE-1774](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1774.md) (Read). A game-theoretic model of a recommender platform that runs an online-learning (adversarial linear contextual bandit) algorithm, recommending one producer per arriving user, while P non-myopic, discounting producers choose a D-dimensional content vector at every step, paying cost \|\|p\|\|^c and earning 1 when recommended. Content quality is measured as producer effort \|\|p\|\| and as user welfare E[<u, p>]. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-1871](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1871.md) | Linear attention is a fast weight programmer | Schlag, Irie & Schmidhuber (2021), [LIT-2642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2642.md), read in [NOTE-1988](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1988.md): linear attention is an outer-product fast weight programmer apart from normalisation (a review of Katharopoulos et al. and Ba et al.), so its memory holds at most about d_dot associations before crosstalk (shown on synthetic retrieval), and a delta-rule write with a learned rate does better when keys are reassigned and in an overcapacity language model. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1877](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1877.md) | Modern Hopfield update is transformer attention | Ramsauer et al. (2020; venue reported as ICLR 2021, unconfirmed), [LIT-2651](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2651.md), read in [NOTE-1952](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1952.md): a continuous modern Hopfield network whose one-step update is softmax attention, with proved convergence, exponential capacity for random patterns and one-step retrieval for separated ones. The theorems are carried as stated; the proofs, in a roughly 90-page appendix, were not read. It says what one attention step computes, not that trained keys act as attractors. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2190](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2190.md) | Hyperbolic cones make embeddings compatible | Bui, Yang, Chen, Neves, Ju, Ying, Shah & Zhao (2025), [LIT-2989](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2989.md), read in [NOTE-2281](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2281.md). Temporal cone restriction as a soft regularizer, and it works. The sharp edges: the hinge is weighted 0.3 and cone satisfaction is never reported; the cones are per item, between two separately trained models; one run per configuration; and the clipping radius must rise at every update, which the authors list as a limitation and which follows from the cone geometry ([CLAIM-860](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-860.md)). Proposed until replicated. | Proposed |
